newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African long bonds ended off the day's best levels on Friday as hopes of an early cut in interest rates, sparked by a surprise drop in first quarter GDP, started to evaporate, dealers said.

The market initially built on Thursday's 20 basis point advance but the benchmark R150 government stock failed to pierce the 14.80 percent level, finishing at 14.86, a gain of just two basis points on the day.

Economists said pressure was building on Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals to cut rates after the surprise 0.8 percent drop in GDP. But most did not expect him to move until the impact of the July 1 easing of exchange controls on individuals could be assessed.

Nonetheless, the conclusion of hectic week for data -- including trade, inflation, money supply, credit extension and GDP -- was that prospects for a rate cut had improved, even if it only comes towards the end of the third quarter.
That should be bullish for bonds next week, some dealers argued.
"The guys took profits ahead of the weekend but they will come in again on Monday and I think it's got the potential to get down to 14.75," one bond trader said.

Better U.S. Treasuries, where the 30-year T-bond yield moved back below the seven percent level, contributed to early gains on the local market. But T-bonds' further advance in the afternoon in delayed reaction to U.S. GDP failed to inspire local players further.
Monday will see the release of May headline official gold and foreign exchange reserves, the main domestic indicator of the week.

Economists polled by Reuters forecast a sharp rise in reserves to 17.70 billion rand from April's 14.40 billion. But this increase mainly reflects well-flagged inflows from the part privatisation of state telecommunications concern Telkom, so the good number may already have been discounted.
Foreigners were net sellers of 140.46 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Thursday after selling 109.19 million rand's worth on Wednesday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal exchange turnover was a massive 40.47 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement date -- from 4.95 billion rand on Wednesday.
On the forex market the rand ended little changed from its overnight levels after retracing early gains.
"We saw good two-way trade with both exporters and importers in, but importers just won the day," said one currency dealer.
The rand was last changing hands at 4.4700/4730 against 4.4670/4.4700 late on Thursday.
In cross rate action, the rand was last changing hands at 0.3805/3810 to the mark from 0.3796/3800 previously.
The local unit was trading at 25.9736/26.013 yen from 25.9441/9839 yen before and 7.3250/3344 to the British pound from 7.3214/3308 before.
Three-month NCD rates remained unchanged from Thursday at 16.35 percent offered, as did 90-day BA rates which lined up at 15.85 percent.
South Africa's money market shortage edged higher to 7.228 billion rand on Thursday from 6.491 billion rand on Wednesday, the Reserve Bank said.
